title: Mesh Hop
summary: Full-screen MeshCore messenger for the deck: chats, contacts, nearby nodes, repeater login and radio settings, with the node on USB, Bluetooth LE or Wi-Fi, by touch or keyboard, on any screen from 640x480 up.
description: A full-screen client for MeshCore LoRa mesh networks. The deck controls a MeshCore companion radio board (the radio is on the board, the deck is the screen and keyboard), reached over USB, Bluetooth LE (paired with its PIN) or Wi-Fi (by its IP address). It opens on Choose a node: one list of the USB boards plugged in, the Bluetooth nodes a short scan hears (with their signal) and the nodes added by IP address; nothing connects by itself, the node chosen last is highlighted. Then a Home list (Chats, Contacts, Tools, Settings, and Node to choose another node); each page has a header with an Esc button. Chats (one pane on 640x480: the list, then the conversation; two side by side on the wider screens; channels and direct conversations with their last message and unread counts, a Search / Add channel bar, the options of a chat (mute, delete, details) by a 3 s hold on its row or Ctrl+O, search in the whole message archive by words, chat, dates and direction), a Contacts list with a Search (a part of the name, or < and the start of the key) you can filter by type, time since heard and group and sort by name, heard, type, SNR, hops or distance, a More menu (send an advert, flood or zero-hop; Nearby; Manage contacts with bulk delete one by one with a progress box and groups); a tap opens a contact by its type (a repeater or room its Repeater page, a chat contact its conversation, a sensor its details) and a 3 s hold (or I) its options (Manage, Message, Details, Groups, Delete); contact details (key, route, last advert, position). The Repeater page logs in to a repeater or room with a masked password (remembered on the deck in the CLI's own password file) or as a guest, shows the role and the repeater's clock, reads its status, neighbours and owner (each on a screen of its own, with Refresh), logs out, and opens the CLI already pointed at it. Tools: a Nearby list of the nodes heard (adverts, pending contacts, an active zero-hop scan, Add and Ignore), a statistics screen, a packet log of the radio packets heard (kept in memory only) and the CLI. Settings: my contact (the node name and its public key), board status with its position (a Position box sets it by hand or with the board GPS switch), node name, radio presets (26 built in, refreshed from api.meshcore.nz in the background when the deck is online), bandwidth, spreading factor, coding rate, TX power and the path hash size (1, 2 or 3 bytes) chosen in a popup with arrows, repeat on or off where the board allows it, a scheduled advert, manual add mode and the auto-add types, direct message retries, board clock, board GPS switch, hashtag and private channels, reboot and factory reset of the board (double confirmation), a History section. A CLI page (Tools > CLI) runs the bundled upstream meshcore-cli 1.6.6 on the connected node, for example to administer your repeaters, while Chats keep their messages; open it from a repeater's page, or from Tools, and it is already pointed at the node you picked in your contacts. Your channel messages show "heard back by N repeaters" when they come back from the mesh. Messages, contacts, groups and flags are kept between runs, separately for each board (by its public key), in ~/.local/share/mesh-hop. Everything works by touch or by keyboard. Text is typed with a Bluetooth or USB keyboard, or with the launcher's on-screen keyboard while none is connected (tap the field); the Esc button of a page goes back to Home, the one of Home asks to quit, and Tab goes to the next page (Chats, Contacts, Tools, Settings). The layout follows the screen (tested at 640x480, 800x480, 720x720, 1024x600 and 1280x720). The board must run a MeshCore companion radio firmware (USB, BLE or Wi-Fi build); for USB the user must be in the dialout group; Bluetooth needs BlueZ (recommended by the package). Needs a screen of at least 640x480 and a launcher with full-screen app support (X-Fullscreen in .desktop files).
